title: [Chapitre] VIII. Analysis situs (quatrième mouture) : notes manuscrites (26/06-04/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (pp. 70-72). Grothendieck is building an 'abstract' theory of figures for his Analysis situs. M is a set of 'figures' carrying a disjointness relation ‖. He assumes a faithful 'cartesian immersion' X ↦ |X| from M to subsets of a point-set P. On p. 70 he asks whether the complete lattice Σ_M attached to M can be realised inside 𝒫(P), so that its order is induced by inclusion and it is stable under arbitrary sup and inf. The stated motivation is to treat cases that are not quasi-set-theoretic, such as 'cordes'.

This page.
(1) He replaces |X| by the finer map φ(X) = |X|°, an 'open support' or interior. His hypothesis is X ‖ Y ⟺ |X|° ∩ |Y|° = ∅: disjointness of figures comes from the inequality relation x ≠ y on P.
(2) He extends φ to subsets A ⊂ M by φ(A) = ⋃_{X∈A} φ(X). Then A ‖ B ⟺ φ(A) ∩ φ(B) = ∅.
(3) He defines the polar co-pr°(A) = {X ∈ M | X ‖ A} = {X | φ(X) ⊂ P∖φ(A)}. The elements S of Σ_M are exactly such polars: the ‖-closed, Galois-closed subsets of M.
(4) For S = co-pr°(A) he gets φ(S) ⊂ P∖φ(A). He asserts, parenthetically, equality.
(5) Key lemma: for such S, X ∈ S ⟺ φ(X) ⊂ φ(S).
- (⇒) is tautological.
- (⇐): φ(X) ⊂ φ(S) ⊂ P∖φ(A) gives φ(X) ∩ φ(A) = ∅, i.e. X ‖ A, so X ∈ S.
(6) Consequence (p. 72): S ↦ φ(S) = |S|° is an injective, order-reflecting map Σ_M → 𝒫(P). It has the left inverse Q ↦ {X | φ(X) ⊂ Q}, the right adjoint of the union map φ.

In modern terms, φ_* ⊣ φ^* is a Galois connection between 𝒫(M) and 𝒫(P). Σ_M, the complete ortholattice of ⊥-closed sets of an orthogonality space, is embedded as a retract of 𝒫(P).

In the topological model the |X|° are open sets. φ(S) is then the union of figure-interiors contained in the closed set P∖φ(A). Under a covering hypothesis this is the interior of P∖φ(A), so Σ_M becomes the Boolean algebra of regular open sets. The realisation preserves arbitrary infs only up to this interior operation. It is not a sub-complete-lattice of 𝒫(P) for unions, which matches the counter-sketch on p. 72 (A ∩ B = ∅ but |A| ∩ |B| ≠ ∅).

The page serves the question raised on p. 70: can the 'lattice of open figures' Σ_M be concretely realised by subsets of a point space?
errors: The parenthetical claim φ(S) = P∖φ(A) is not justified by the stated hypotheses. φ(S) is only the union of those φ(X) that lie inside P∖φ(A). Equality requires a covering or density hypothesis (every point of P∖φ(A) lies in some |X|° disjoint from φ(A)). In topological models it fails: one only gets the interior of the complement. Only the inclusion ⊂ is proved, and only the inclusion is needed for the injectivity lemma.

Injectivity gives an order-embedding and retraction, but not stability under arbitrary sups in 𝒫(P). That was the desideratum on p. 70 and is not achieved here; the next page's sketch suggests he noticed this.

ideas.what: Disjointness relation on figures induced from point-disjointness of open supports; polar co-pr°(A) and the lattice Σ_M of ‖-closed sets
ideas.modern_name: orthogonality space / Birkhoff polarity; complete ortholattice of biorthogonally closed sets

ideas.what: Union map φ(A)=⋃|X|° and its right adjoint Q ↦ {X | |X|° ⊂ Q}; injectivity of Σ_M → 𝒫(P) via X∈S ⟺ φ(X)⊂φ(S)
ideas.modern_name: Galois connection / adjunction; closed elements embed as a retract
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ore (1944), standard lattice theory; cf. formal concept analysis (Wille 1982)

ideas.what: Implicit identification of Σ_M with regular-open-type sets in the point model
ideas.modern_name: regular open algebra; point-free topology (frames/locales, Boolean algebra of regular opens)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Stone, Tarski (1930s); locale theory (Ehresmann, Isbell, Johnstone)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a correct but standard Galois-connection/polarity argument, embedding the lattice of orthogonally closed sets into a power set. It is of mild historical interest as part of the 1986 Analysis situs effort toward point-free 'figures', but contains nothing new to a specialist.
transcription_corrections: The operator written 'co-ψ°' is more plausibly 'co-pr°' (cf. 'X ∈ co-pr°A' in the last line and 's-pr°' on p. 72), i.e. a co-/polar operator rather than ψ.
'S' under-braces mark the set later called S; 'connait [?] ... ⊂ [?]' is roughly 'est connu par la partie φ(S) ⊂ P∖φ(A) de P (et = à P∖φ(A)), par X∈S ⟺ φ(X)⊂φ(S)'.
Last bracket: 'φ(X) ⊂ φ(S) implique φ(X) ⊂ P∖φ(A), i.e. φ(X) ∩ φ(A) = ∅, i.e. X ‖ A donc X ∈ co-pr°A'.
